findings.fix: Add a control inside the "invite-sent" section whose target is another state the artifact defines, for example a back, cancel, or continue control.
findings.violation: This state offers no control whose target names another state the artifact defines, so a user who reaches it has no path to leave it within the artifact.
findings.evidence: the "invite-sent" section defines 0 controls whose target names another defined state (1 incoming link from elsewhere in the artifact).

findings.fix: Add visible text to this control, or an aria-label attribute naming what it does.
findings.violation: This control has neither visible text nor an accessible-name attribute, so nothing on screen names what the control does.
findings.evidence: <button> with no text content and no accessible-name attribute

findings.fix: Add a success message displayed after the user clicks Save, or show a changed control state such as the button becoming disabled briefly or the form showing a save confirmation.
findings.violation: This state-changing action (saving the project name) lacks a specified visible indication of outcome, so the user cannot tell whether the save succeeded or failed.
findings.evidence: The form contains a text input labeled "Project name" with current value "Design System Refresh" and a "Save" button; the artifact specifies no feedback message, loading state, or changed control appearance after clicking Save.

findings.fix: Add a success message displayed after clicking Save, or show the form returning to a default state that confirms the change was saved.
findings.violation: This state-changing action (saving notification settings) lacks a specified visible indication of outcome, so the user cannot tell whether the save succeeded.
findings.evidence: The form contains a select dropdown labeled "Digest frequency" and a "Save" button; the artifact specifies no feedback message or control state change after clicking Save.

findings.fix: Add a control in the invite-sent screen or a follow-up screen to revoke or cancel the sent invite, or document that sent invites cannot be recalled.
findings.violation: Sending an invite is a committed action; the artifact provides no named reversal path or undo mechanism.
findings.evidence: After the invite is sent and the user reaches the "Invite sent" screen, the artifact states "An invite was sent to the address entered above. It expires in 5 days if not accepted." No control or documented path to revoke, cancel, or unsend the invite appears anywhere in the artifact.

findings.fix: Mark the currently selected option with a selected attribute in the HTML, or show the current digest frequency selection before presenting the form options.
findings.violation: The user cannot see what the current digest frequency setting is when arriving at the notification-settings screen, so they lack information needed to make an informed decision about whether to change it.
findings.evidence: The select element lists "Daily" and "Weekly" options with no indication of which is currently selected; the HTML markup shows no selected attribute and no other visual indicator of the current setting.
